column1: # The "critical pure-core" class set of TASK-007: the logic that has no Android
# framework excuse for being untested, and the JVM test class that answers for it.
# Why an owner column exists at all: a line counter cannot tell a class that a
# test set out to exercise from one that happened to execute because something
# else called it. The owner is the single test class that carries this class
# past the floor with nothing else running, which is what
# verifyPureCoreAttribution re-measures. It is therefore the test responsible
# for the coverage, which is not always the test named after the class, and an
# owner is not a promise that the class has a test of its own.
# NONE means no single test class carries it: either nothing exercises the
# class at all, or its coverage is spread so thin across unrelated tests that
# none of them would be missed. That is a recorded gap, not a formality:
# verifyPureCoreCoverage fails on it until a test claims the class. Never
# invent an owner to silence the gate, and never record one that
# Format: three tab-separated columns, comments and blank lines ignored.
#   1. class         JaCoCo class name, slash form, no package-less shorthand.
#                    Inner and synthetic classes (names containing '$') are
#                    outside the set and must not be listed.
#   2. owner_test    fully qualified JVM test class, dot form, or NONE.
#   3. owner_module  Gradle path of the module holding owner_test, or - for NONE.
